title: Double embouchure and who used it
summary: Discussion of the double embouchure used by Barney Bigard, Manuel Manetta and Sam Dutrey, and why Hall doubts it.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: That's been, oh, a couple of years. 56. Yeah, only 56. Do you know anybody that used that? Like, do you remember any of the, of course the TOs, I guess, weren't here when you came here, they were through, except Lorenzo went to New York.

But you knew, do you know anybody that used the double embouchure? I just heard about that, I just heard about that not so very long ago, who that double embouchure because you see who it was, some famous kind of people was going to some teaching trying to use that double.

In Europe, I think some of the French classical symphony men do that, in France especially, is what I read once years ago, 20 years ago. But I'd never known anybody personally, except Barney Bigard, and then Manuel Moneta said he did it that way, and his teacher, Sam Doudre, who used to play on the boat with Louis in 1918 or so, his brother was with King Oliver's band, and anyway, Sam Doudre advised everybody to use that double embouchure.

Use the two of them to help you put your feet up. Well I guess you'd have double of trouble, then like you'd stop playing for about, say a couple of weeks and you'd go back, because both lips get sore. Yeah, sure.
When I first started playing, if I practiced for, let's say a couple of hours, I'd make it bleed. That's right, you make it sore. Sure.
